images.title: Crossing out multiples of 2
images.purpose: Show one step of the sieve: circle 2 and cross out its multiples.
images.composition: One row of 10 equal number boxes, centred, with a short note below.
images.exact_structure: One row of exactly 10 equal square boxes numbered 1 to 10, evenly spaced. Box 1 has a grey #6B7280 cross. Box 2 has a teal #0072B2 circle. Boxes 4, 6, 8 and 10 each have a grey cross. Boxes 3, 5, 7 and 9 are plain. Below, centred: one short note. Exactly 10 boxes, 1 circle, 5 crosses.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any number other than 1, 4, 6, 8, 10 crossed, or any box other than 2 circled
images.takeaway: Circle a prime, then cross out all of its multiples.
images.description: Boxes 1 to 10 in a row: 2 circled in teal, 1 and the multiples 4, 6, 8, 10 crossed in grey, 3, 5, 7, 9 plain.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say which number they would circle next.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
